Folks around Knox Country always believed the forest provided cures as well as dangers.
Recent culinary experiments may finally explain why.

POISONOUS MUSHROOMS
Hunters and trappers have long claimed that tiny amounts of poisonous mushrooms could “clean” spoiled meat during cooking.
Surprisingly, recent studies suggest there may be some truth to those old wilderness tales.

LEMON GRASS
Its bitter oils and strong aroma have made lemon grass a favorite among wilderness cooks for generations. Some even believe it helps make questionable meals easier on the stomach.

[ON THE LEFT]
Lost in the woods with nothing left but some unknown source meat you found?
Improperly prepared meat may carry dangerous contamination.

[ON THE RIGHT]
Veteran survivalist Bob Fletcher shares one of his favorite wilderness cooking tricks.

A SIMPLE RECIPE THAT MAY SAVE YOUR LIFE
Take some dubious meat. Mix it with some wild poisonous mushrooms and a few sprigs of lemon grass. Now cook thoroughly for best results.

Knowledge Keeps You Alive!

[HANDWROTE IN THE BACK OF THE FLYER IN SMALL LETTERS]
Who the fuck would believe this shit?.
